tests.name: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage
tests.description: Review JS files, HTML comments, source map files for secrets, credentials, internal paths.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively flags JS files with sensitive strings; limited JS analysis depth. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-105.10. robots.txt/sitemap.xml internal-path disclosure -- implemented in disclosure_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: page.evaluate() to extract all script src URLs; run SecretFinder against each.

tests.name: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files
tests.description: Find backup files (.bak, .old, .zip, .sql) and unreferenced resources with sensitive data.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner checks common backup paths; limited wordlist coverage. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-105.5. Source map / VCS / backup file left exposed on the webserver -- implemented in disclosure_tests.py, verified live against demo.testfire.net.]
tests.automation_approach: dirsearch subprocess with backup wordlist; requests.get() per URL through Burp proxy.

tests.name: Web Cache Poisoning
tests.description: Exploit web cache behaviour to store and serve malicious HTTP responses to users.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Web Cache Poisoning Scanner (via param-miner extension detects cache headers). [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-136.1. Web cache poisoning via unkeyed header injection -- implemented in cache_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Burp Param Miner extension + custom requests with X-Forwarded-Host, X-Original-URL headers.

tests.name: Web Cache Deception
tests.description: Trick web cache to store authenticated pages under cacheable URL paths.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp detects cache headers; manual path manipulation needed to confirm cache deception. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-136.2. Web cache deception via static-resource-shaped path suffix -- implemented in cache_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: requests.get('/profile/test.css') with auth cookie; check if unauthenticated user gets cached version.

tests.name: Default Configuration Check
tests.description: Check if components use factory/default configurations (credentials, endpoints, services). Includes TC-017.6: CORS misconfiguration where the server dynamically reflects an attacker-supplied Origin back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Includes TC-017.7: Content-Security-Policy missing or weak on text/html responses only (no CSP header, unsafe-inline without a nonce/hash source, unsafe-eval, or a bare */data:/https: script source) -- a strict default-src 'self' policy is never flagged. Includes TC-017.8: missing clickjacking (X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors) or MIME-sniffing (X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff) headers on text/html responses. Includes TC-017.9: TLS/transport analysis -- a sensitive (login/auth/session/payment-shaped) endpoint reachable over plaintext http://, or an HTTPS target missing Strict-Transport-Security. Includes TC-017.10: publicly-listable cloud storage (S3/Azure Blob/GCS) referenced by the target, confirmed via an object-listing XML/JSON body signature, never status code alone. HTTP-method analysis (OPTIONS/Allow-header enumeration) was researched but not built -- disclosed-report evidence for it stays weak as a standalone finding, usually cited only alongside a real PUT/DELETE exploitation writeup (see configuration_knowledge_base.json).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner checks default files and endpoints; limited to known patterns.
tests.automation_approach: ffuf with SecLists/Passwords/Default-Credentials wordlist against login endpoint.

tests.name: Test Role Definitions
tests.description: Validate system roles by creating permission matrix; ensure least privilege enforced.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot assess role definition logic without app context. [GAP: needs a full RBAC permission-matrix build (login as every configured role, assert access per discovered endpoint) -- a genuinely new capability beyond this codebase's existing per-technique role-tamper checks (TC-056), not yet built. Left undone rather than rushed.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: login as each role; build RBAC matrix; assert endpoint accessibility per role.

tests.name: Test Account Provisioning Process
tests.description: Determine which roles can provision users and what account types they can create.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot assess account provisioning workflow logic. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-135.1 / TC-135.2. Account provisioning process: reserved-username acceptance + self-assigned privilege at registration -- implemented in business_logic_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: attempt user provisioning as non-admin; assert 403 response.

tests.name: Testing for Weak or Unenforced Username Policy
tests.description: Check if usernames follow predictable pattern; test for enumerable account names.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder can enumerate usernames; response diff analysis. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-022.5. Username enumeration via the login endpoint's own response differential -- implemented in auth_tests.py. Also covered from the reset-endpoint angle by TC-027.5.]
tests.automation_approach: ffuf username enumeration against login endpoint with username wordlist.

tests.name: Testing for Default Credentials
tests.description: Test application for default factory credentials (admin/admin, admin/password etc.).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder with credential wordlist; no automated default cred DB built-in.
tests.automation_approach: requests.post(login_url, data={user: cred[0], pass: cred[1]}) for each pair in SecLists/Default-Credentials.

tests.name: Testing for Weak Lock Out Mechanism
tests.description: Evaluate lockout after N failed attempts; test unlock mechanism resistance.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder can send multiple failed logins; lockout detection is manual. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.11. Login lockout bypass via spoofed X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: loop N+1 failed logins; assert account locks; test unlock path.

tests.name: Testing for Bypassing Authentication Schema
tests.description: Forced browsing, parameter modification, session ID prediction, SQL injection in auth.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner detects SQL injection in auth; forced browsing via Spider.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: navigate directly to post-login URLs without session; assert redirect to login.

tests.name: Testing for Weak Password Policy
tests.description: Evaluate password length, complexity, reuse, aging requirements via dictionary attack.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder dictionary attack; no policy enforcement check built-in.
tests.automation_approach: requests.post(login_url) with SecLists password wordlist through Burp proxy.

tests.name: Testing for Weak Security Question and Answer
tests.description: Check if security answers are predictable, blank, or brute-forcible.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot assess security question logic without app-specific context.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: walk security question/answer flow; test blank/common answers.

tests.name: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
tests.description: Test reset token entropy, expiry, reuse; old sessions invalidated post-reset; CSRF.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp detects CSRF in reset flow; token analysis is manual.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: drive reset flow; capture token; test reuse after use; test expired token.

tests.name: Email/OTP Flooding
tests.description: Check if OTPs/emails can be generated in bulk (flood attack) to cause DoS or spam.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder can send repeated OTP requests; response analysis is manual.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: loop OTP trigger endpoint 50+ times; assert rate limit kicks in.

tests.name: OTP Validation
tests.description: Check if OTP is properly validated server-side; test expired/reused OTPs.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot intercept out-of-band OTP channels (SMS/email).
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: capture OTP; replay same OTP after use; test OTP after expiry window.

tests.name: OTP / 2FA Bypass
tests.description: Check if 2FA service can be bypassed by skipping, replaying, or manipulating OTP flow.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot automatically bypass 2FA; requires manual session manipulation.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: after password step, navigate directly to post-2FA URL; test response manipulation.

tests.name: Testing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
tests.description: Identify MFA type; assess robustness; attempt bypass; test backup code flows.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot drive MFA flows without manual token entry. [Phase 2, per this project's own CLAUDE.md rule 9: MFA/OAuth/SAML auth flows are explicitly deferred, not in Phase 1 scope even if requested -- stof/auth/mfa.py exists as a stub for when that phase starts.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept OTP channel (mock); drive full MFA flow; test skip and replay attacks.

tests.name: Testing for Bypassing Authentication Schema (Web)
tests.description: Force browsing to authenticated pages; parameter modification; session ID prediction.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner detects some auth bypass; forced browsing via Spider.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: navigate to /admin/*, /dashboard without auth; assert 302/401/403.

tests.name: Auto-complete Enabled on Sensitive Fields
tests.description: Check if autocomplete is ON for username and password input fields.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively flags autocomplete on password fields. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-017.13. Password autocomplete gap -- implemented in configuration_tests.py (Info severity by design, defense-in-depth only).]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: page.query_selector('input[autocomplete]'); assert 'off' or 'new-password'.

tests.name: Concurrent Sessions
tests.description: Login same user from multiple browsers; check if application allows concurrent sessions.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot manage multiple simultaneous sessions natively. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.7. Concurrent sessions not revoked on second login -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: open 2 browser contexts; login same user in both; assert second login invalidates first.

tests.name: Cross Service Relay Attack
tests.description: Check if audience claim in JWT is correctly validated to prevent cross-service token reuse.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot automatically test JWT audience claims across services.
tests.automation_approach: jwt-pwn: decode token; modify 'aud' claim; replay to different service endpoint.

tests.name: Testing for Logout Functionality
tests.description: Verify server-side session invalidation on logout; test SSO session termination.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp can replay old session tokens post-logout; manual verification needed.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: logout; capture old session token; replay to protected endpoint; assert 401.

tests.name: Session Timeout / Never Expires
tests.description: Validate hard session timeout; inactivity timeout; token destruction post-expiry.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp can detect long-lived tokens; timeout verification requires time-based testing.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: login; idle for configured period; attempt action; assert 401 or redirect.

tests.name: Session Hijacking
tests.description: Identify vulnerable session cookies; test theft and reuse via XSS or network sniffing.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp can replay captured tokens; XSS-based hijacking detection via Scanner. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.13. Session not bound to client fingerprint (User-Agent swap replay) -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: inject XSS payload; capture cookie; replay in new context; assert access.

tests.name: Testing for Session Puzzling
tests.description: Identify session variables reused across different app contexts; break logical flow.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot automatically identify session variable reuse across contexts. [GAP: session puzzling (mixing state from two different multi-step flows, e.g. MFA/reset) has no safe, generic black-box test without deep app-specific flow knowledge -- risks false positives if forced. Left undone rather than rushed; revisit if a target with a multi-step auth flow is in scope.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: map all session variable usage across app flows; test cross-context reuse.

tests.name: Back and Refresh Attack
tests.description: Sign out and press browser back button to check if session is accessible again.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot simulate browser back/forward navigation behaviour. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.9. Authenticated response missing no-store/no-cache Cache-Control (back/refresh cache weakness) -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: logout; page.go_back(); assert page content is not loaded (redirect to login).

tests.name: Broken Access Control
tests.description: Access restrictions fail; test all protected endpoints with unauthenticated requests.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Autorize extension: automatic session swap testing; active scanner checks some ACL.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: crawl with admin; replay all requests with user/unauth session via Burp Autorize.

tests.name: Bypassing Authorization Schema
tests.description: Access resources without auth; bypass ACL; force browsing (/admin/adduser.jsp).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner + Autorize: partial detection; forced browsing via Spider. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-055.1-.5. Bypassing function-level authorization schema (forced browsing, verb tampering, hidden endpoints, role-differential matrix) -- implemented in bfla_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: attempt admin URLs as standard user; assert each returns 403.

tests.name: Privilege Escalation
tests.description: Manipulate role/privilege hidden variables; change groupid=2 to groupid=1.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder can fuzz role parameters; Autorize detects role-based bypass.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept requests; modify role/group params; assert server validates server-side.

tests.name: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR)
tests.description: Force change parameter value (?invoice=123 → ?invoice=456) to access other objects. Also analyzes (TC-053.6, non-probing) whether discovered object ids are structurally sequential/enumerable integers versus properly random UUIDs/tokens -- a contributing risk factor independent of any single confirmed IDOR.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Autorize + IDOR Scanner extension; manual ID enumeration via Intruder.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: capture object IDs; replay with incremented IDs using other user session.

tests.name: Missing Object-Level Authorization (BOLA)
tests.description: No ownership validation; User A accesses User B's objects via manipulated IDs.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Autorize cross-user replay; BOLA detection requires multi-session context.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: multi-context (User A + User B); User B requests User A's object IDs.

tests.name: Missing Function-Level Authorization (BFLA)
tests.description: Protected functions exposed to lower-privilege users; admin functions callable by users.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Autorize function replay; Scanner checks some endpoint authorization.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: enumerate all function endpoints as admin; replay each with user token.

tests.name: Role Manipulation
tests.description: User modifies role value in request body, cookie, or JWT to escalate privileges.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder fuzzes role values; JWT manipulation needs extension.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept and modify role field; jwt-pwn for JWT role claim rewrite.

tests.name: JWT Role Manipulation
tests.description: Modify JWT role claim (user→admin); test alg=none, weak HMAC secret, algorithm confusion attacks; validate exp/nbf/iat/iss/aud claim enforcement (TC-057.5); test token replay after logout (TC-057.6); scan for JWT exposure in URLs/browser storage (TC-057.7); inject the 'kid' header claim -- path traversal to a known-empty file re-signed with its content, and a SQLi-shaped value checked for a DB-error fingerprint (TC-057.8).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp JWT Editor extension: full alg-confusion, none-attack, key confusion.
tests.automation_approach: jwtXploiter: test alg=none, RS256→HS256, kid injection; replay forged tokens through Burp.

tests.name: JWT Token Validation
tests.description: Verify token expiry, signature, claims (iss, aud, exp) are properly validated server-side.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp JWT Editor extension: modify claims, strip signature, test each attack type. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-057.1. JWT signature-tamper validation -- implemented in jwt_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: jwt-pwn: decode; modify exp claim to past; replay; assert rejection. Test none algorithm.

tests.name: JWT Vulnerable KID Parameter
tests.description: Test KID header for SQL injection, path traversal, command injection.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp JWT Editor: modify KID; Scanner may catch SQL injection in KID. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-057.4. JWT JWKS/kid confusion -- implemented in jwt_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: jwt-pwn: set kid to SQL payload; set kid to '../../../dev/null'; replay and check response.

tests.name: SQL Injection via JWT KID
tests.description: UNION-based and blind SQL injection via JWT Key ID parameter.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp JWT Editor + Scanner can detect SQLi in KID; manual payload crafting needed. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-057.3. JWT weak-secret brute force (HMAC) -- implemented in jwt_tests.py. (SQLi-via-kid specifically not covered -- narrower than this entry.)]
tests.automation_approach: jwt-pwn: set kid=' OR '1'='1; replay; check response for SQL error or data disclosure.

tests.name: Billion Laughs / XML Bomb
tests.description: XML entity expansion attack causing excessive resource consumption (DoS).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner may detect XXE; XML bomb specific test is manual. [Declined: this is a real denial-of-service technique (uncontrolled resource consumption) against a live target -- out of scope for an automated tool to fire without a specific, authorized DoS test window agreed with the target owner, regardless of severity label.]
tests.automation_approach: requests.post(endpoint, data=xml_bomb_payload) through Burp; monitor response time.

tests.name: Mass Assignment
tests.description: Inject extra fields (role, isAdmin, privilege_level) into PUT/PATCH request body.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner: partial mass assignment; manual param injection via Repeater. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-052.4. Escalation via mass assignment (role/isAdmin injection on profile update) -- implemented in mass_assignment_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept PUT/PATCH; inject {'role':'admin','isAdmin':true}; assert server rejects.

tests.name: DOM-Based XSS
tests.description: Malicious DOM manipulation via document.write, innerHTML, eval on user-controlled input.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner detects some DOM XSS; deep JS analysis limited. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-128.5. DOM-based XSS via real in-browser confirm() dialog-fire confirmation -- implemented in xss_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Burp DOM Invader extension; Playwright: inject payload in URL fragment; observe DOM changes.

tests.name: CSS Injection
tests.description: Inject CSS code to exfiltrate data via CSS selectors or execute JavaScript via expression().
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner: limited CSS injection detection; mainly flags XSS surface. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-128.7. CSS Injection via attribute-context breakout -- implemented in xss_tests.py, reuses TC-128.2's unencoded-reflection oracle.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: inject CSS selectors; monitor outbound requests for data exfiltration.

tests.name: HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP)
tests.description: Duplicate parameters to bypass input validation filters (?user_id=legit&user_id=victim).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder with HPP payloads; active scanner limited HPP detection. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-134.1. HTTP Parameter Pollution -- implemented in injection_variants_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept and duplicate sensitive params; Burp Param Miner extension.

tests.name: Excessive Data Exposure
tests.description: API returns more data than needed; frontend filters sensitive fields not server-side.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively identifies PII/sensitive fields in responses; manual analysis needed. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-105.9. Excessive data exposure via sensitive JSON field names -- implemented in disclosure_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept API responses; compare JSON fields against expected schema; flag extras.

tests.name: Sensitive Data Exposure in Error Messages
tests.description: Error messages reveal stack traces, DB queries, framework versions, internal paths.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner triggers errors and checks responses; passive detection of stack traces. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-105.2. PII leaked via error messages / stack traces -- implemented in disclosure_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: trigger 404/500 errors; assert response doesn't contain stack trace or DB info.

tests.name: Insecure Deserialization
tests.description: Modify serialized objects (Java, PHP, Python) to execute arbitrary code or modify behavior. STOF's own coverage is deliberately payload-free: TC-085.4 adds a passive structural check for ASP.NET ViewState rendered without a __VIEWSTATEMAC field (MAC validation disabled), the documented precondition for ViewState deserialization RCE; TC-085.5 is a purely passive content-type/format discovery check (Java-serialization magic-byte fingerprint in an already-crawled parameter value, or a serialization-format Content-Type on a single harmless GET); TC-085.6 fingerprints a serialization library name+version from response headers only (no probe payload) -- alongside TC-085.2's benign polymorphic-type-marker probe. TC-085.1 (gadget-chain RCE) and TC-085.3 (DoS) remain permanently not implemented by design.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner + Deserialization extensions (Java Deserialization Scanner, GadgetProbe).
tests.automation_approach: Burp Java Deserialization Scanner extension; ysoserial payloads via Burp Intruder.

tests.name: Export Injection
tests.description: Inject HTML/iframe tags into data export flows (PDF, CSV) to read arbitrary files.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner cannot detect export-specific injection chains.
tests.automation_approach: requests.post(export_url, data={'name': '<iframe src=/etc/passwd>'}); check exported file content.

tests.name: CSV Injection
tests.description: Inject formula code (=cmd|...) into CSV exports to execute code when file is opened.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner cannot detect CSV formula injection. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-134.2. CSV/Formula Injection -- implemented in injection_variants_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: input =DDE("cmd","/c calc","",,) in text field; export CSV; check file for formulas.

tests.name: DoS via Parameter Manipulation
tests.description: Manipulate limit/page parameters to request excessive data causing Layer 7 DoS.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner detects some DoS vectors; large payload testing via Intruder. [Declined: same reasoning as TC-070 -- an intentionally excessive-resource-consumption request is a real DoS technique, not a safe generic probe.]
tests.automation_approach: requests.get('/api/data?limit=999999999') through Burp; monitor response time.

tests.name: Business Logic Authorization Bypass
tests.description: Workflow authorization missing; skip approval stages in multi-step processes.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot assess application-specific business logic without app knowledge. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-135.3. Business-logic authorization bypass via workflow step skipping -- implemented in business_logic_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: navigate directly to workflow step 3 URL skipping steps 1 and 2.

tests.name: Workflow Step Skipping
tests.description: Navigate directly to later workflow steps bypassing approval/verification stages.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot model application workflow state machine. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-135.3. Workflow step skipping -- implemented in business_logic_tests.py (same technique as TC-093).]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: load workflow step URLs from YAML; skip to final step; assert server blocks.

tests.name: Approval Process Bypass
tests.description: Submit transaction and directly call approve endpoint without approver action.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot understand approver workflow without app context.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: as initiator, submit txn; directly POST /api/approve/{txn_id}; assert 403.

tests.name: Race Condition Privilege Escalation
tests.description: Timing attack exploits non-atomic privilege check and action window.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Turbo Intruder: HTTP/2 single-packet race condition attacks. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-135.4. Race condition on a limited-use endpoint via concurrent duplicate submission -- implemented in business_logic_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Turbo Intruder single-packet race; asyncio.gather() for HTTP/1.1 parallel requests.

tests.name: Test for Process Timing
tests.description: Identify timing vulnerabilities that allow prediction or circumvention of business logic.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot model timing-based business logic without app-specific knowledge. [GAP: a black-box timing oracle (e.g. username-enumeration-via-response-time) needs statistical sampling across many requests against a stable network baseline to separate a real timing signal from ordinary jitter -- a single-shot generic probe would be prone to false positives/negatives on a real target's network. Left undone rather than rushed.]
tests.automation_approach: Turbo Intruder: measure response time variance; identify timing oracles.

tests.name: Test Function Usage Limits
tests.description: Functions executable more times than business logic allows (discount reuse, coupon replay).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot enforce or test business-defined function limits. [Implemented as STOF's own generic technique TC-135.5 (business_logic_tests.py): fires the same request 3x sequentially at a discovered redeem/claim/vote/coupon-shaped endpoint and checks whether a later call is rejected.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: call function N+1 times; assert server rejects after limit.

tests.name: Malicious File Upload
tests.description: Upload malicious files (web shells, executables) bypassing type/content validation.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner: file upload vulnerability checks; manual payload variation needed. [GAP: needs crawler support for detecting <input type=file>/multipart form fields, which doesn't exist yet -- a prerequisite change, not a single technique. Left undone rather than rushed.] [Implemented as STOF's own generic technique TC-099.1 (file_upload_tests.py): the crawler now tags <input type=file> fields (form_detector.py's param_locations, additive-only), and this technique uploads a marker file with a server-executable extension (.php/.phtml/.jsp/.asp) disguised with a benign Content-Type, checking whether it's accepted with no rejection signal. STOF never retrieves/executes the uploaded file to confirm actual code execution -- acceptance alone is the signal, real exploitation confirmation is a manual follow-up step.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: upload test files (shell.php, test.phtml, shell.PhP); assert rejection.

tests.name: Unrestricted File Upload
tests.description: Test file type, size, MIME type, double extension, path traversal in file names.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner: file upload bypass techniques; MIME type analysis. [GAP: same prerequisite as TC-099 (no file-input detection in the crawler yet).] [Implemented as STOF's own generic technique TC-100.1 (file_upload_tests.py): same crawler prerequisite as TC-099, testing a double-extension bypass (shell.php.jpg / shell.jpg.php) instead of a single dangerous extension.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: test boundary cases (10MB file, .phtml ext, null byte in filename).

tests.name: Test Payment Functionality
tests.description: Check if transaction IDs, OTP, account numbers are encrypted; test negative amounts.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot verify payment encryption or business logic without context. [GAP: negative-amount/quantity tampering needs to already know a target's valid price/quantity schema to pick a value that's genuinely wrong -- this project's business_logic_tests.py module docstring documents this exact tradeoff (false positives/negatives either way) and deliberately does not build a generic version. Left undone rather than rushed; a human pentester with app context is the right owner for this one.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: drive payment flow; intercept; test negative amounts; assert encryption of sensitive fields.

tests.name: Sensitive Data Leakage in Response
tests.description: API returns full data objects; PII, secrets, internal IDs exposed in responses.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively identifies PII patterns in responses; limited by pattern matching. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-105.1 / TC-105.4. PII present in API response / URLs / logs -- implemented in disclosure_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept API responses; parse JSON; check for PII fields against allowed schema.

tests.name: PII Exposure via API
tests.description: APIs return raw PII (SSN, card numbers, emails, DOB) without field-level filtering. Also covers source map/VCS/backup file exposure (TC-105.5), PII/secrets hidden in HTML comments or inline scripts (TC-105.6), and PII/secrets left in localStorage/sessionStorage after authentication (TC-105.7).
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively flags PII patterns; Scanner response analysis.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: intercept all API responses; run regex for SSN, card numbers, email; flag matches.

tests.name: Rate Limiting
tests.description: Check rate limiting implementation; test X-Rate-Limit header bypass techniques.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder: send burst requests; check response for rate limit headers. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.10. Rate limiting on password-reset requests (the sensitive non-login endpoint TC-107 names) -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py, extends TC-129.3's login-rate-limit check.]
tests.automation_approach: Turbo Intruder: send 200 requests in 1 second; assert 429 Too Many Requests response.

tests.name: Rate Limit on Token Level
tests.description: Verify rate limiting applied at token/user level; test max retry and jail mechanism.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Intruder: per-token burst; limited automation for token-level rate limit. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-129.12. Rate limiting at the authenticated API/token level -- implemented in session_weakness_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: Turbo Intruder with Authorization header rotation; count 429s per token.

tests.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Misconfiguration
tests.description: Analyze CSP header for unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, overly permissive origins.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively detects missing CSP; CSP analysis needs manual review. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-017.7. CSP missing/weak on HTML responses -- implemented in configuration_tests.py, verified with false-positive guards (nonce/hash sources, strict policies).]
tests.automation_approach: requests.get(url).headers['Content-Security-Policy']; CSP evaluator tool.

tests.name: GraphQL Introspection Enabled
tests.description: Query GraphQL introspection endpoint to enumerate full schema in production.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp InQL extension: full GraphQL introspection and schema enumeration. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-116.5. GraphQL introspection enabled -- implemented in graphql_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: InQL: run introspection query; extract all types, queries, mutations; identify sensitive resolvers.

tests.name: GraphQL Authorization Bypass
tests.description: Resolver authorization missing; access other users' data via GraphQL queries, mutations, batched aliasing, or nested/relational field traversal; introspection exposure scored separately as its own (TC-116.5) informational finding.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp InQL + Autorize: replay GraphQL mutations with low-privilege token.
tests.automation_approach: InQL: enumerate resolvers; test each with user token vs admin token; compare responses.

tests.name: OAuth Weak redirect_uri Configuration
tests.description: Test for open redirect via manipulated redirect_uri; verify strict whitelist enforcement.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner detects open redirect; OAuth-specific testing is manual. [Phase 2, per this project's own CLAUDE.md rule 9: OAuth flows are explicitly deferred, not in Phase 1 scope even if requested -- stof/auth/oauth.py exists as a stub for when that phase starts.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: modify redirect_uri to attacker URL; check if authorization server allows redirect.

tests.name: OAuth Leaking Authorization Codes/Tokens
tests.description: Authorization codes/tokens exposed in referrer, browser history, logs.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively detects tokens in URL/Referer headers.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: monitor Referer headers in page.on('request'); check for token leakage.

tests.name: Logging Failed Logins Server-Side
tests.description: Confirm server logs failed login attempts with sufficient context.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp cannot access server-side logs directly. [GAP: this needs read access to the target's own server-side logs, which a black-box scanner never has by design -- there is no external signal STOF could observe to confirm a failed login was actually logged server-side. Left undone; this is inherently a code/config review item, not a DAST check.]
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: generate N failed logins; query /admin/logs API; assert entries exist.

tests.name: GraphQL Batching Attack
tests.description: Combine multiple queries in one batch request to bypass rate limiting or DoS server.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner cannot natively detect GraphQL batching attacks. [STOF coverage: implemented as TC-116.3. GraphQL batched-query authorization bypass -- implemented in graphql_tests.py.]
tests.automation_approach: requests.post(gql_url, json=[{query1}, {query2}...{query100}]); check rate limit bypass.

tests.name: SQL Injection
tests.description: Inject crafted values into discovered query/body parameters, JSON API request bodies, request headers, an authorized non-auth cookie, and free-text-storage POST fields (and the login form) to detect error-based, boolean-blind, time-based blind, header-based, cookie-based, JSON-body, second-order (stored/cross-endpoint), and login-bypass SQL injection -- signal detection only, never real data extraction.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: inject a small curated payload set per discovered parameter (and the login form's username/password fields); classify error-based via a DB-error fingerprint, boolean-blind via a true/false response-similarity differential, time-based via one bounded 2s-capped sleep payload confirmed once, login-bypass via an authenticated-looking response vs. a wrong-credentials baseline, header-based by placing the same error-based payloads into User-Agent/X-Forwarded-For/Referer, second-order via a plant-then-verify pair (a low-priv POST into a free-text field, then a separate high-priv GET against a likely-privileged endpoint checked for a DB-error fingerprint) gated behind allow_state_changing_probes.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner's own SQLi checks cover this generically; STOF's version is target-agnostic and reuses the same discovered-endpoint/param map every other module here reads from.

tests.name: Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected, Stored, DOM-based) + Related Client-Side Injection
tests.description: 9 techniques: Reflected XSS across 3 injection contexts (raw HTML body, HTML attribute breakout, inline script/event-handler breakout -- TC-128.1-.3), Stored XSS via a plant-then-verify pair across a low-priv and high-priv context (TC-128.4), DOM-based XSS with real in-browser execution confirmation via a page.on('dialog') listener, not just response inspection (TC-128.5), DOM-based Open Redirect (TC-128.6), CSS Injection via attribute-context breakout (TC-128.7), DOM Data Manipulation where a client-controlled value reaches a storage/attribute sink (TC-128.8), and HTML Injection via unencoded markup reflection with no script/event-handler content (TC-128.9). Every payload carries a unique per-run marker so a hit can never be confused with stale data from a previous scan.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: inject a uniquely-tagged marker payload per discovered parameter, per context variant (raw HTML body, HTML attribute, inline script/event-handler), and check the response for an unencoded (not HTML-entity-escaped) reflection in an executable position. Stored XSS (TC-128.4) is a plant-then-verify pair (a low-priv POST into a free-text field, then a separate high-priv GET against a likely-privileged endpoint checked for an unencoded reflection of the planted marker) gated behind allow_state_changing_probes, same shape as TC-127.6's second-order SQLi technique. DOM-based XSS (TC-128.5) is the one technique in this test case that performs real browser navigation instead of response inspection: it appends the marker payload to location.hash and location.search on a bounded set of discovered endpoints and reports a FAIL only when a page.on('dialog') listener observes an actually-triggered confirm() dialog whose message contains this run's own marker -- genuine proof of execution, not a signal consistent with one. TC-128.6/.7/.8/.9 reuse the same discovered-endpoint/param map and marker-uniqueness convention, varying only the payload shape and the oracle context.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner's own reflected-XSS checks cover this generically; STOF's version reuses the same discovered-endpoint/param map every other module here reads from.

tests.name: Session / Rate-Limit Weaknesses
tests.description: Session identifier not regenerated on login (fixation), session cookie remains valid after logout, no rate limiting/lockout across repeated failed login attempts, session remains valid after a password change, (TC-129.5) a newly-issued/changed session/auth cookie missing HttpOnly, Secure, or a safe SameSite value, (TC-129.6) session timeout/expiry not observable or unbounded -- a deliberately honest structural check of Session.expires_at, not a fabricated live-wait test, since actually waiting out a real inactivity/absolute timeout window is impractical inside a bounded scan, (TC-129.7) a prior session is not revoked when a second login completes for the same account, and (TC-129.8) the session token is low-entropy or predictable across independent logins (short value, shared prefix, sequential numeric pattern, or low character-set variety) -- signal detection only, via a small bounded probe set.
tests.compliance: OWASP WSTG-SESS-03; WSTG-SESS-06; WSTG-SESS-07; WSTG-ATHN-03; ASVS 3.2; ASVS 3.3; ASVS 2.2
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: diff an anonymous pre-login cookie value against the same-named post-login cookie (fixation); capture a session cookie, trigger logout, and replay the old cookie against a known page (post-logout validity); loop 5-8 wrong-credential login attempts against distinct made-up usernames and check for an HTTP 429/CAPTCHA/lockout signal (rate limiting); TC-129.5: identify the session/auth cookie as whichever cookie is NEW or CHANGED between an anonymous pre-login context and a freshly-authenticated context, then check HttpOnly (first priority), Secure (https targets only), and SameSite=None-without-Secure -- SameSite simply absent is never flagged; TC-129.6: force a fresh login and inspect the resulting Session.expires_at against Session.created_at, SKIPping cleanly (never a fabricated PASS/FAIL) when no expiry is observable, FAILing when the observed span exceeds a generous 24h bound; TC-129.7: two real logins for the same role, then replay the FIRST login's cookies after the SECOND completes -- a still-authenticated response means concurrent sessions are not revoked; TC-129.8: compare the SAME-named session cookie's value across those same two independent logins for a shared prefix, sequential numeric pattern, short length, or low character-set variety.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp passively flags session cookies not marked HttpOnly/Secure and can be scripted (Intruder) for a login-attempt burst; the fixation/post-logout-validity comparisons and the automated pass/fail judgement are STOF-specific.

tests.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
tests.description: A discovered state-changing POST endpoint has no anti-CSRF token field at all, succeeds with the token field stripped from the request, succeeds with a spoofed cross-site Origin/Referer, or succeeds when the anti-CSRF token was harvested from a DIFFERENT authenticated role's own session (token not bound to the presenting session) -- signal detection only, using only the test account's own legitimate-shaped data. Also checks whether the session cookie's SameSite attribute meaningfully protects this endpoint from CSRF (SameSite=None is always flagged; SameSite=Lax/absent is only flagged when this same endpoint also has no anti-CSRF token AND doesn't validate Origin/Referer -- a compounding-risk signal, not a restatement of the separate session-hijacking cookie-flag check), and whether a discovered JSON-body API endpoint's protection survives being resubmitted as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (a content-type a plain HTML form can produce without JavaScript), which SKIPs cleanly on targets with no JSON-body API endpoint. Skips any role authenticated via a bearer token/header (auth_type "jwt"), which isn't CSRF-exploitable; the token-not-bound-to-session check additionally needs a second, distinct, non-JWT role configured and skips cleanly otherwise.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: submit a discovered state-changing form/POST endpoint as normal (baseline token field present), then again with the token field stripped, then again with a spoofed Origin/Referer header using the role's real cookies; a still-200/success response on either probe is the finding.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner flags missing/predictable CSRF tokens passively; the strip-and-replay and Origin/Referer-spoof confirmation probes and the automated pass/fail judgement are STOF-specific.

tests.name: Tenant Isolation BOLA (organization/tenant-scope parameter substitution)
tests.description: A discovered GET/POST endpoint carries an organization/tenant/company/workspace-scoping parameter (distinct from a per-object identifier); substituting this project's configured candidate ids into it and comparing response content across candidates checks whether the server validates session legitimacy but not organizational membership -- the tenant_isolation family in stof/payloads/idor_knowledge_base.json (8.3% of real-world disclosed BOLA reports, zero prior STOF coverage).
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: identify GET/POST endpoints with a single org_id/organization_id/tenant_id/tenantid/company_id/workspace_id-shaped parameter; substitute IdorTestConfig.candidate_ids into it; apply the same content-differential confirmation (_probe_candidates/_content_fingerprint) idor_tests.py already uses for object-id substitution. POST-based substitution requires IdorTestConfig.allow_state_changing_probes, same gate as every other write-verb technique in this file family.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Autorize can replay a captured request with a modified parameter, but does not itself recognise a tenant/org-scope parameter as distinct from an object id -- that classification and the automated pass/fail judgement are STOF-specific.

tests.name: Weak Security Question/Answer
tests.description: Discovery-first check of whether this target's account-recovery/verification flow uses security questions at all -- scans discovered forms/pages for a security-question-shaped field (name/id hints: securityQuestion, secretAnswer, recoveryQuestion, kbaQuestion, ...). SKIPs cleanly when no such flow exists (the honest, expected outcome on most modern targets, which use email/SMS OTP instead). When found, classifies the question's own visible text against a small curated list of WSTG-cited low-entropy examples (mother's maiden name, first pet, favorite color, high school, city of birth, ...) and FAILs (Medium) only on an actual match -- never attempts to guess or submit an answer, and never claims a specific answer was tested.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: find a discovered endpoint whose parameters match a security-question-shaped field-name hint list; GET that page and search its visible body text against a small curated list of known low-entropy question patterns from WSTG's own AUTHN-09 examples; FAIL only on a real match, SKIP when no security-question flow is discovered at all.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner has no built-in classifier for security-question quality; this is a purely STOF-specific discovery-and-classification technique, grounded directly in WSTG-AUTHN-09's own methodology rather than bug-bounty disclosure evidence.

tests.name: Authentication Schema Bypass
tests.description: Tests whether the AUTHENTICATION check itself -- not the identity/role behind it -- can be dodged by varying the request's SHAPE alone, entirely unauthenticated. Distinct from this project's existing IDOR/BFLA forced-browsing techniques, which test authorization gaps for an authenticated-but-wrong-role caller. Takes a small, bounded set of already-discovered auth-required GET endpoints; for each whose unmodified URL correctly denies an anonymous baseline request, generates a small bounded list of shape variants (case-flip of the last path segment, trailing slash, trailing dot, a `;jsessionid=` path-parameter suffix, a URL-encoded null byte) and requests each anonymously. FAILs (High) if any variant returns authenticated-looking content where the baseline correctly denied it; SKIPs an endpoint whose baseline is already anonymously reachable (a plain forced-browsing gap, not this technique's case) rather than false-PASSing it.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: for each of up to 5 discovered auth-required GET endpoints, GET the unmodified URL anonymously as a baseline (redirect/401/403/login-page body = correctly denied); if denied, GET each of a bounded set of request-shape variants (path case-flip, trailing slash/dot, jsessionid/null-byte suffix) anonymously and check for authenticated-looking content (dashboard/logout/welcome markers) in an HTTP 200 response -- a still-denied baseline with a bypassed variant is the finding.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp's own path-normalization/discrepancy checks (in newer Scanner versions) can surface some of these shape variants passively; the systematic bounded variant sweep against every discovered auth-required endpoint and the automated pass/fail judgement are STOF-specific, grounded in WSTG-AUTHN-04's own methodology.

tests.name: Injection Variants -- HPP, CSV Formula, Command Injection, XXE, SSTI, NoSQL Injection
tests.description: TC-134.1: a discovered endpoint's parameter is submitted twice in one request (duplicate query-string or form-body key) and the response is compared against two SEPARATE single-value baselines (first value alone, second value alone) -- flags only when the polluted response reflects BOTH values together, or matches NEITHER baseline, evidence of inconsistent parameter parsing across the request-processing stack (WSTG-INPV-04) worth manual review, not a confirmed exploit. TC-134.2: a harmless, formula-shaped marker ('=1+1+"stofcsv<marker>"') is planted into a discovered free-text POST field as a low-priv user, then a separate, higher-privileged GET context checks whether the stored value survives verbatim -- reported honestly as "would survive into a CSV/Excel export unescaped IF one exists" (CWE-1236). TC-134.3 (WSTG-INPV-12): a bounded, repeatable-before-reporting shell sleep payload (4 separator styles tried per candidate: ;, |, $(), backtick) into a discovered parameter, flagged only on a confirmed repeatable timing delta. TC-134.4 (WSTG-INPV-07): re-submits a discovered POST endpoint with an XML body declaring an external entity pointing at a low-sensitivity file (/etc/hostname), differential-checked against a no-entity baseline, with an XML/entity-parser-error fingerprint as a lower-confidence fallback. TC-134.5: a polyglot arithmetic-expression payload spanning Jinja2/Twig/Freemarker/Thymeleaf/ERB syntax with this run's own random operands, flagged only when the computed product appears while the raw payload text does not (proof of server-side template evaluation). TC-134.6: a discovered JSON login endpoint's password field is substituted with a MongoDB operator object ($ne/$gt) instead of a string, flagged only on an actually-authenticated-looking result.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: TC-134.1 sends baseline_a (param=A), baseline_b (param=B), then a duplicate-key polluted request (param=A&param=B) via a raw query-string/form-body build (dict params can't express duplicate keys), diffing the polluted response against both baselines with SequenceMatcher; gated behind allow_state_changing_probes since the POST variant resubmits a discovered form. TC-134.2 reuses sqli_tests.py's/xss_tests.py's own _second_order_plant_candidates/_second_order_verify_candidates plant/verify helpers from _injection_shared.py; gated behind allow_state_changing_probes since the plant phase is a real POST. TC-134.3 mirrors sqli_tests.py's TC-127.3 time-based-blind shape (baseline, payload, confirm-once) across 4 shell-separator styles, stopping at the first repeatable hit. TC-134.4 sends a raw XML body via a new _send_raw_body helper (send_probe's dict-params interface can't express a raw non-form/non-JSON body), differential-checked at the entity-substitution boundary. TC-134.5 reuses injectable_endpoints/build_params/send_probe unchanged, only the payload and evaluation-signal oracle are new. TC-134.6 reuses find_login_endpoint (base.py) and looks_json_authenticated (_injection_shared.py, both already built for TC-127.4) unchanged, building the JSON body directly (json.dumps) to carry a nested operator object a dict[str, str]-typed params mapping can't express.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner can flag reflected parameter pollution and CSV export issues are largely out of its passive-scan scope; the differential baseline comparison and the plant/verify cross-role CSV-survival check are STOF-specific.

tests.name: Business Logic / Identity Testing
tests.description: TC-135.1 (WSTG-IDNT-02): if the crawler discovered a self-service registration form, submits a small set of reserved/system usernames (admin, administrator, root, support) and FAILs (Medium) if any is accepted instead of rejected. TC-135.2 (WSTG-IDNT-01): if that registration form itself exposes a role/privilege-shaped field, submits it with an elevated value on an anonymous signup and FAILs (Critical) if the elevated value is honored and echoed back. TC-135.3 (WSTG-BUSL): if the crawler discovered 2+ endpoints that look like sequential steps of one flow (shared path prefix, a step/stage-shaped query param or path segment), requests the latest step directly, anonymously, without completing the earlier step(s) first, and FAILs (High) if it is reachable. TC-135.7 (WSTG-BUSL, workflow state-machine modeling): for a richer 3+ step flow, models the FULL ordered chain of steps and probes every intermediate/terminal one independently (not just the last), reporting exactly which specific steps are reachable out of order -- a deeper pass than TC-135.3's single last-step check. Deliberately does not attempt price/quantity/discount/cart manipulation (WSTG-BUSL's other sub-cases) -- those require target-specific schema knowledge a generic scanner cannot safely infer; see stof/modules/business_logic_tests.py's module docstring.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: TC-135.1/.2 POST a fully-filled registration payload (matching the form's own declared parameter names) to the discovered registration endpoint from a fresh anonymous context; TC-135.3 GETs the latest-step endpoint of a discovered multi-step flow directly from a fresh anonymous context. All three gated behind allow_state_changing_probes since each is a real, state-creating/state-skipping request against the live target.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Business logic flaws are inherently outside Burp Scanner's automated signature-based detection; this is manual-testing territory Burp explicitly does not automate.

tests.name: Web Cache Poisoning & Web Cache Deception
tests.description: TC-136.1 (PortSwigger Practical Web Cache Poisoning): identifies a discovered response carrying a cache-indicating header (Cache-Control/X-Cache/Age/ETag), sends a request with an 'unkeyed' header (X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-Scheme/X-Forwarded-Proto) set to a synthetic .invalid-TLD marker, and only FAILs (High) if a SEPARATE, unmodified follow-up request also observes that marker -- proving the poisoned response was actually cached and served back out, not just reflected once. TC-136.2 (PortSwigger Web Cache Deception): appends a static-resource-shaped suffix (/nonexistent.css) to a discovered authenticated/sensitive page, checks whether the server ignores the suffix and the response looks cacheable, then confirms with a SEPARATE, fully anonymous request to the same suffixed URL -- FAILs (High) only if that anonymous request receives the first, authenticated request's real content. Both techniques could affect a real shared cache serving other, unrelated visitors -- a materially larger blast radius than any other technique in this project -- and are gated behind allow_state_changing_probes in their entirety, including the read-only cache-header reconnaissance step.
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: TC-136.1 probes a bounded set of discovered GET endpoints for a cache-indicating header, then sends a request with each of 3 unkeyed headers set to a unique synthetic marker, confirming reflection via a second, separate unmodified request. TC-136.2 diffs an authenticated GET's body fingerprint (SHA-256) against a suffixed variant of the same URL, then a fully anonymous request to that suffixed URL, requiring an exact fingerprint match on both to confirm.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp's Web Cache Poisoning extension and Web Security Academy labs cover this manually; the automated bounded unkeyed-header sweep with genuine two-request confirmation, and the automated authenticated-vs-anonymous fingerprint diff for deception, are STOF-specific.

tests.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
tests.description: TC-137.1 (WSTG-INPV-19): injects a URL-shaped parameter with AWS's instance-metadata endpoint and a loopback URL, diffing each response against a baseline request to a guaranteed-unreachable RFC 2606 .invalid host; FAILs only when the internal-target response both differs meaningfully from that failure baseline AND carries a recognizable metadata field-name signature. TC-137.2: PortSwigger's own documented blind-SSRF-without-a-collaborator technique -- points the parameter at a well-known non-routable address and measures whether the response takes a dramatically, repeatably longer time than a same-shaped baseline, evidence the server actually attempted an outbound connection and blocked on its own connect-timeout. TC-137.3: injects a file:///etc/passwd payload and checks for the 'root:x:0:0' fingerprint absent from the baseline, confirming the fetcher honors non-HTTP(S) schemes. TC-137.4: the same baseline-diff oracle swept across a small, curated list of commonly-exposed internal service ports (SSH, MySQL, Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch, two alt-HTTP/admin ports) on 127.0.0.1, distinguishing 'loopback reachable at all' from 'which internal services specifically respond'. TC-137.5: the IP/hostname parsing bypass sub-class -- only fires when the plain loopback URL is already confirmed blocked, then retries the identical destination as decimal/octal/hex IP notation, shortened dotted-decimal, IPv6 loopback, and IPv4-mapped IPv6; a signal on any alternate encoding where the plain form showed none is direct evidence of an allowlist that checks the URL string rather than its resolved destination. TC-137.6: an operator-configured out-of-band collaborator (config.json's burp.collaborator_url, set via the UI's Settings -> Out-of-band testing) lets this technique send a genuine unique-per-probe OOB callback URL into every candidate parameter -- the strongest confirmation technique for true blind SSRF (a webhook/async fetch with neither a timing nor content signal). STOF does not poll the collaborator's own API for a received callback, so this reports SKIPPED with the exact markers sent, not a FAIL/PASS it can't verify -- checking the collaborator's dashboard is the human confirmation step. Redirect-based allowlist bypass and DNS-rebinding remain out of scope -- both need STOF's own attacker-controlled redirect/DNS infrastructure to test honestly; see stof/modules/ssrf_tests.py's module docstring for the full scoping rationale.
tests.source_checklist: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG); PortSwigger Web Security Academy
tests.automation_approach: Playwright: for each URL-shaped discovered parameter (url/uri/link/webhook/callback/redirect/image/... hint list), sends the parameter's own baseline request to a guaranteed-unreachable RFC 2606 .invalid host, then diffs cloud-metadata/loopback/non-routable/file-scheme probes against that baseline using response-similarity ratio and timing deltas -- no out-of-band collaborator required for any of the three techniques.
tests.burp_coverage_notes: Burp Scanner's own SSRF detection primarily relies on Burp Collaborator (OAST); the timing-oracle and metadata-fingerprint techniques here are collaborator-free alternatives, genuinely complementary rather than a strict superset or subset of Burp's own coverage.
